description: Gathers four separate signals into one polyphonic cable, and splits a polyphonic cable back into four separate signals, in two sections that are not connected to each other

inputs.text: Becomes the polyphonic channel of that number at the merge output
The polyphonic signal whose channels are sent out separately

outputs.text: Carries the four merge inputs as one four-channel polyphonic signal
Carries the channel of that number from the split input, on its own

notes: merging a signal, quantizing it and splitting it again adds three sample delays to the pitch path; the SampleDelays modules can put the same delay on a gate path
a merge input left empty below a patched one takes a channel of the merge output all the same, and that channel carries 0V
menu: Channels Merge — sets how many channels the merge output carries: Automatic, the default, gives as many channels as the highest-numbered patched merge input, or choose a fixed count from 1 to 4
